findings.guide_says: A buildup of 1/8" (3mm) or more calls for cleaning by a chimney professional, and possibly a change in how you burn and more frequent checks.
findings.manual_says: Owner's Manual p. 6: "The presence in a chimney of soot or creosote in excess of 1/8" (3mm) thick will indicate the need for immediate cleaning, possible modification of burning procedures, and more frequent inspections." (p. 16: "A buildup of 1/8" (3mm) or more calls for cleaning by a chimney professional.") The drawer merges the two pages and drops "immediate".
findings.fix: A buildup of 1/8" (3mm) or more calls for immediate cleaning by a chimney professional, and possibly a change in how you burn and more frequent checks.

findings.guide_says: Never use gasoline, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or any other flammable liquid to start or refresh the fire.
findings.manual_says: Owner's Manual p. 4, item 9: "DO NOT ever use gasoline, gasoline-type lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or freshen up a fire. Keep all such liquids well away from the fireplace while it is in use." The second sentence of the warning is dropped.
findings.fix: Add to the danger note: "Keep all such liquids well away from the fireplace while it's in use."

findings.guide_says: Left partly open, air rushes in and over-fires the fireplace, which can permanently damage it.
findings.manual_says: Owner's Manual p. 9 (same wording p. 4, item 4): "If the glass door is left partly open, it will increase the burn rate and permanently damage the fireplace." and "DO NOT BURN THE FIREPLACE WITH THE DOOR PARTIALLY OPEN. AIR WILL RUSH INTO THE FIREBOX AND CAUSE THE FIREPLACE TO OVERFIRE." The guide softens "will" to "can".
findings.fix: Never burn with it partly open: air rushes in, the burn rate goes up and the fireplace over-fires, which will permanently damage it.

findings.guide_says: Use a cleaner your dealer recommends; wood stove glass cleaners work far better than regular glass or oven cleaners.
findings.manual_says: Owner's Manual p. 13: "NEVER CLEAN THE GLASS WITH AN ABRASIVE CLEANER. USE ONLY A CLEANER RECOMMENDED BY YOUR DEALER." The guide drops "only", which turns a restriction into a suggestion.
findings.fix: Use only a cleaner your dealer recommends; wood stove glass cleaners work far better than regular glass or oven cleaners.

findings.guide_says: Densified wood logs: no more than two at a time, firescreen closed. Wax logs (like Duraflame): one at a time, firescreen closed. (No condition on which firelogs may be used.)
findings.manual_says: Owner's Manual p. 8, same section: "Use only firelogs that have been evaluated for fireplace use. In Canada, they must meet the requirements of ANSI/CAN/UL/ULC 2115 Processed Solid Fuel Firelogs and Firestarter. Refer to the firelog warnings and caution markings on packaging prior to use."
findings.fix: After the wax-log bullet add: "Use only firelogs evaluated for fireplace use (in Canada they must meet ANSI/CAN/UL/ULC 2115), and read the warnings on the package before you use them."

findings.guide_says: Vented flashing (RF-12RVF) is required if the chimney is in a chase or enclosed to the roof; don't caulk its vents.
findings.manual_says: Install p. 33 text: "A vented flashing (RF-12RVF) MUST be used if the chimney is in a chase or is enclosed to the roof." Table 9 on the same page heads its columns "Regular Flashing US and Canada | Vented Flashing US only | Vented Flashing Canada only" and lists RF-12RVF (0/12), RF-12RVFA (4/12) and RF-12RVFB (10/12) under US only, and RF-12RCVF / RF-12RCVFA / RF-12RCVFB under Canada only. The guide covers Canadian installs but names only the US low-pitch part. (Part-number-to-pitch reading follows the table layout; check it against the page image.)
findings.fix: Vented flashing is required if the chimney is in a chase or enclosed to the roof; don't caulk its vents. The text names RF-12RVF; Table 9 lists RF-12RVF, RF-12RVFA or RF-12RVFB by roof pitch for the US and RF-12RCVF, RF-12RCVFA or RF-12RCVFB for Canada.

findings.guide_says: Card: "Door open, screen closed 3.4 g/kg", "Door closed 0.68 g/kg", "Typical burn rate 5.9 kg/hr" (note: ASTM 2558 test protocol). Drawer gives the same figures plus 3.95 g/hr, then: "Emission rates per the ASTM 2558 test protocol. When lined with the optional vermiculite panels, it has met the EPA Voluntary Wood Burning Fireplace Program Phase 2 emission level."
findings.manual_says: Install p. 8 (Owner's p. 6 identical): "When lined with the optional vermiculite panels, it has met the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Voluntary Wood Burning Fireplace Program Phase 2 emission level. It is: Typically burning at a rate of 5.9 kg/hr, Clean burning with an emission rate of 3.4 g/kg when burned with the door open and the firescreen closed ... 0.68 g/kg when burned with the door closed ... 3.95 g/hr when burned with the door closed." The figures are listed under the vermiculite-lining condition; no figures are given for the EO-RB1500 cement refractory brick lining. The guide shows them as figures for the fireplace in general.
findings.fix: Tie the figures to the lining: card note "ASTM 2558 test protocol; with vermiculite panels (EO-VP1500)", and in the drawer put the vermiculite sentence ahead of the rows: "Lined with the optional vermiculite panels, it has met the EPA Voluntary Wood Burning Fireplace Program Phase 2 emission level, with these figures:".

findings.guide_says: The remaining framing dimensions are shown only on the Figure 3 drawing on this page, and the fireplace dimensions only on Figure 2 (p. 9). (No Maker's website note.)
findings.manual_says: Install p. 9 has only the drawing "FIGURE 2 FIREPLACE DIMENSIONS"; no dimension appears in the text. website.json prints Outside Dimensions: 59⅛" W X 87¾" H X 32½" D. GUIDE_SPEC (website section): where the manual gives a figure only in a drawing, the website's figures go where the guide points to the drawing.
findings.fix:
After the Figure 2 sentence add
Maker's website: Outside Dimensions 59⅛" W X 87¾" H X 32½" D. Install to the dimension drawing in the manual.
and record it in review.catalog_mismatches with "shown": "specFrame".

verdict: Yes: every clearance, chimney, hearth, mantel, outside-air and fuel-load number, all 28 page links and all 8 notes match the manuals and website, so after these eight minor wording and qualifier fixes the guide is safe to publish.
